newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude premiums flat but Jan/Feb dips to +20.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude premiums flat but Jan/Feb dips to +20.

text.p: Premiums for North Sea wet crudes remained steady in afternoon trading on Friday but intermonth spreads crumbled as a pivotal trade at 20 cents a barrel for January above February undermined the market.
Although the spread talked either side of 22 cents later, it was still some way off Thursday's trade on the same spread traded at 35 cents a barrel.
Despite the weaker intermonth and CFD values most premiums held steady with Brent trading at 20 cents a barrel over February twice and Oseberg trading at 45 cents above Dated Brent.

An Jan 14 Oseberg traded at 45 cents over Brent but with a deferred pricing which meant an equivalent price of 38 or 39 cents above Brent. At least one other Oseberg traded loading around Jan 10, perhaps as part of a spread against Ekofisk, said traders. A Jan 23-25 Forties was heard sold at Dated Brent +42 cents, steady from levels talked earlier this week.

Two of five sets of Brent dates were unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline, but some traders saw the chance of a recovery in premiums next week. "Although there were signs of prompt supplies building up there are also buyers out there who need the oil," said a trader.
"The Osebergs got pretty much cleared out and there wasn't any sign of Urals getting hit," he added.
Other traders had seen widespread offers of Urals cargo loading in the middle decade of January earlier on Friday.

In the Mediterranean, Urals talked a touch firmer helped by improved refinery margins but a prompt cargo was still offered by a trader at around Dated Brent -$1.10. "There are several cargoes around in both the north and south for the mid-decade (10-20 January)," said a trader.
Feb Brent was still trading about 30 cents a barrel below Thursday's close late in the afternoon.
